items.followUp: Define molecular formula and explain how it differs from an empirical formula.

rubric.why: The definition must identify that an empirical formula gives the simplest whole-number ratio of atoms of each element.
rubric.description: Defines an empirical formula as the simplest whole-number ratio of the atoms of each element in a compound.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct definition conveying the simplest whole-number ratio of atoms of each element.

rubric.why: A method for determining the formula is required.
rubric.description: Explains that amounts of elements are converted to moles and their ratio is reduced to the simplest whole numbers.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining the conversion to moles and simplification of the mole ratio.

modelAnswer: An empirical formula represents the simplest whole-number ratio of the atoms of each element in a compound.
It is determined from the composition by converting the amounts of the elements to moles and reducing their mole ratio to the simplest whole numbers.

items.followUp: Define electron affinity and write an equation showing the electron affinity of chlorine.

rubric.why: The definition must describe energy release when a gaseous atom accepts an electron and forms a negative ion.
rubric.description: Defines electron affinity as the energy released when a neutral gaseous atom accepts an electron to form a negative ion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a definition that includes energy release, electron acceptance, and negative-ion formation.

rubric.why: A suitable example must show chlorine accepting an electron to form a chloride ion.
rubric.description: Gives chlorine accepting an electron to form a chloride ion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the chlorine example, expressed in words or as a correct reaction.

modelAnswer: Electron affinity is the energy released when a neutral gaseous atom accepts an electron to form a negative ion.
For example, a chlorine atom accepts an electron to form a chloride ion: Cl(g) + e⁻ → Cl⁻(g) + energy.

items.followUp: Define a covalent bond and give one example.

rubric.why: An ionic bond is the attraction between oppositely charged ions.
rubric.description: Defines an ionic bond as the electrostatic force of attraction between oppositely charged ions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged ions.

rubric.why: A correct example of an ionic compound is required.
rubric.description: Gives sodium chloride (NaCl) as an example of an ionic compound.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid example such as sodium chloride.

modelAnswer: An ionic bond is the electrostatic force of attraction between oppositely charged ions.
Sodium chloride (NaCl) is an example of an ionic compound.
